root_cause.text: On UP kernels, spin_trylock() is a no-op that always succeeds, so an NMI handler calling alloc_frozen_pages_nolock() can re-enter rmqueue() and acquire the zone lock already held by the interrupted context, corrupting freelists.
root_cause.evidence: Commit message explicitly states: "On UP kernels (!CONFIG_SMP), spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds even when the lock is already held. As a result, alloc_frozen_pages_nolock() called from NMI context can re-enter rmqueue() and acquire the zone lock that the interrupted context is already holding, corrupting the freelists." The call trace also confirms NMI entry into alloc_frozen_pages_nolock_noprof then rmqueue, with a spinlock trylock failure. The fix adds a check `if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SMP) && in_nmi()) return NULL;` to prevent this re-entry.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces spin_trylock_irqsave in rmqueue_bulk() and rmqueue_buddy() without any handling for UP kernels where spin_trylock always succeeds. This allows an NMI handler to re-enter and acquire the zone lock already held, leading to freelist corruption. The try_alloc_pages() function calls these paths with ALLOC_TRYLOCK, making it vulnerable.
